text:
sarah-support: heads up — acme reported 429s for /v1/generate starting ~22:10 UTC, but their Console quota panel shows ~20k tokens remaining. screenshot: https://redwood.internal/snapshots/acme-429-22-10.png

sarah-support: quick summary + first customer repro: they hit 429 with request_id rq_acme_20260316_221004. customer says it happens intermittently during bursts.

sarah-support: repro curl we captured:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_acme_XXXX" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":512}'
```
response body:
```json
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","code":429,"details":"burst_quota_exceeded"}}
```

maria-product: how many customers affected? SLA impact? :thinking_face:

ivan-eng: can you paste the internal enforcement log lines for rq_acme_20260316_221004 and the api key? also which plan is sk_acme_XXXX on (org vs api-key level rates)?

sarah-support: api_key=key_acme_42, org_id=org_acme. plan=paid-dedicated-2. attached enforcement log snippet from the time:
```
[2026-03-16T22:10:04Z] rate_limiter:allow=false api_key=key_acme_42 rate=100r/s window=1s tokens_left=-12 req_id=rq_acme_20260316_221004
```

ops-oncall: looking at rate-limiter traces — enforcement uses per-api-key token bucket with 1s bucket and burst allowance. Console counters are driven by the metrics ingestion pipeline which aggregates to org-level per-minute. If ingestion is delayed, Console can show stale "available" tokens even while enforcement already returned 429s.

alex-telemetry: confirmed — our consumer for topic "quota-usage-v2" shows high lag on partition 5 around 22:08-22:20, behind by ~40-50m. That topic feeds the realtime panels in Console. Enforcement writes are synchronous to Redis and go straight to the limiter.

ivan-eng: ok that explains the data staleness, but why did enforcement actually deny? was there a miscalculation or double-counting?

ops-oncall: enforcement logs show a short burst from the customer + another automated client in the same org that spiked concurrently. Token bucket dropped to negative. The dashboard query aggregates daily tokens and also applies org-level quota smoothing — it doesn't represent per-second bursts. So both are technically correct for their surfaces.

maria-product: customer will see 429s and Console showing tokens -> out of sync is confusing. We need a clear customer note + short-term mitigation.

ivan-eng: action items from eng: 1) confirm telemetry consumer restart / backfill; 2) add reconciliation job to compare enforcement counters vs console aggregates; 3) add an explanation blurb in Console about burst vs sustained quotas. I'll take 1 and 2.

alex-telemetry: I restarted the consumer at 22:45 UTC (deploy id consumer-2026-03-16-22-45). Backfill job kicked off, ETA ~25m. Created INC-2345 to track. Grafana (topic lag): https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/quota-topics?from=now-2h

deploy-bot: deployed consumer-2026-03-16-22-45 (rollout id r-8873) to telemetry cluster beta.

ops-oncall: started a one-off reconcile script that scans enforcement logs for the last 3 hours and emits a reconciliation metric. Running now, should finish ~10m. If results show missing events, we'll backfill from raw kafka offset.

sarah-support: I told acme that we're investigating and that 429s can occur during bursts even if Console shows available tokens; offered a temporary bump in burst limit while we reconcile. Customer accepted temp bump, but asked for root cause note.

ivan-eng: low-level root cause preliminary: telemetry consumer group lost its committed offsets on partition 5 due to a bug in the consumer restart path (offsets with colons in the key failed to commit). That caused a 30–50m visibility gap for some api_keys. Fix will be in next patch to the consumer commit logic. Filed ENG-5678.

maria-product: please prepare a short customer-facing postmortem blurb once we have the final RCA and mitigation timeline. Also add UI tooltip to explain per-second bursts vs aggregated Console numbers (UX ticket UX-998).

alex-telemetry: will follow up in INC-2345 with backfill success and final offsets.

ivan-eng: repro steps for engineering to validate locally:
```bash
# synthetic spike to reproduce 429s locally
for i in {1..400}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_burst" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":32}' &
done
# observe enforcement logs for token drops
```

ops-oncall: customer mitigation checklist:
- temporary burst increase applied to key_acme_42 until 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC
- telemetry consumer restarted and backfill in progress
- reconcile script running and alert created if >1% keys mismatched

sarah-support: thanks team — I'll update the customer channel with ETA and keep ops copied.

ivan-eng: follow-ups: ENG-5678 (consumer commit fix), ENG-5679 (reconcile job permanent), UX-998 (console tooltip). I'll own ENG-5678/5679.

alex-telemetry: backfill finished at ~23:05 UTC, Console numbers started to reflect enforcement usage. leaving INC-2345 open until reconcile metrics look green.

maria-product: good work — make sure we get a short summary for the account execs and include the tooltip wording draft.

sarah-support: closing loop with acme now. will post final note when reconcile is green. :white_check_mark:
